nodes.name: Public Presence
nodes.purpose: Enable an agency to build and publish its own front-facing website — the hook for attracting both clients and workers — without writing code.
nodes.ux_intent: Building the agency's front page feels like filling out a beautiful Instagram profile, not configuring a CMS. The result should make a parent or homeowner immediately feel: 'This is a professional agency I can trust.'
nodes.vertical_notes: For caregiving: the front page must convey warmth, trust, and safety — DBS badge, verified status front and centre. For cleaning: professionalism, efficiency, and cleanliness aesthetics. Both should make booking feel zero-effort.
nodes.case_integration: Worker public profiles link to their Case Portfolio pages for richer proof-of-work.
open_questions: Should each worker have a subdomain? e.g., agency.com/nannies/jane

nodes.name: Agency Homepage
nodes.purpose: The agency's primary public-facing page — hero, services, trust signals, testimonials, and a clear booking CTA — rendered for SEO and conversion.
nodes.ux_intent: A visitor lands and within 5 seconds knows: what the agency does, why to trust them, and how to book. Zero friction to conversion.
inputs: org content: hero_text, tagline, service_list, testimonials, team_photos, trust_badges
nodes.vertical_notes: Trust badges: 'DBS-checked staff', 'Insurance covered', 'Ofsted-referenced' (caregiving). 'Fully insured', 'CRB-checked' (cleaning). Hero photo should show real warmth — a nanny reading to a toddler, or a sparkling clean kitchen.

nodes.name: Edit Homepage Content
nodes.purpose: Allow admins to update their homepage content — hero text, tagline, photos, testimonials, and trust badges — through a visual editor without touching code.
nodes.ux_intent: The editor shows a live preview on the right while the admin types on the left — no 'publish then refresh' loop.
nodes.vertical_notes: Admin should be prompted to add a warm personal note from the agency founder — this converts especially well for caregiving parents looking for a human connection.

nodes.name: Publish Homepage
nodes.purpose: Make the current homepage content live on the public-facing URL, with cache invalidation.
nodes.ux_intent: A 'Publish' button with a satisfying animation and a 'Your page is live!' confirmation with a link to view it.

nodes.name: View Public Homepage
nodes.purpose: Serve the SEO-optimised, server-rendered homepage to any visitor — logged in or anonymous.
nodes.ux_intent: Loads in under 1 second. No layout shift. Looks stunning on mobile first.

nodes.name: Worker Directory
nodes.purpose: A public, searchable listing of the agency's available workers — allowing clients to browse profiles before booking.
nodes.ux_intent: Feels like a curated gallery of trusted professionals, not a database query. Each card is warm and human.
inputs: filter: service_type, location, availability, age_groups_supported, specialisms
nodes.vertical_notes: For caregiving: filter by age group speciality (infant, toddler, school-age, elderly), live-in/out, first aid certified. For cleaning: filter by service type (deep clean, end-of-tenancy, commercial), travel zone. Each card shows DBS check status prominently.
nodes.case_integration: Each worker card links to their Case Portfolio profile for full proof-of-work.

nodes.name: List Workers (Directory)
nodes.purpose: Return the paginated, filterable list of public worker profiles for the agency's directory page.
nodes.ux_intent: Results update as the user adjusts filters — no 'search' button, instant feedback.
outputs: WorkerPublicCard[] {name, photo, rating, verified_badges, tagline, specialisms}
nodes.vertical_notes: Workers control their own visibility — if on a long-term placement, they can hide from the directory.

nodes.name: View Worker Public Profile
nodes.purpose: Render the full public profile of a specific worker — experience, verified credentials, ratings, assignment history highlights, and a booking CTA.
nodes.ux_intent: The profile page is the 'sell' moment — it should feel like reading a trusted colleague's LinkedIn plus their Airbnb reviews. Visitors feel confident and compelled to book.
outputs: WorkerPublicProfile{bio, credentials, specialisms, ratings, history_highlights, availability_snippet}
nodes.vertical_notes: Caregiving: prominently show DBS status, First Aid cert, age groups worked with, 'Has worked with X families' count. Cleaning: show DBS status, COSHH cert, 'Has completed X cleans', specialisms (end-of-tenancy, carpet, commercial).
nodes.case_integration: Profile pulls enriched proof items from Case Portfolio (did, trained, vouched, aiming pillars).

nodes.name: Booking Widget
nodes.purpose: An embeddable, frictionless booking flow that can appear on any page of the public site — allowing anonymous or registered clients to request a service in under 2 minutes.
nodes.ux_intent: The booking widget feels like a friendly chatbot conversation, not a form. 'What do you need? When? Where? Great — we'll find someone perfect for you.'
outputs: ServiceRequest created (anon or linked to account)
nodes.vertical_notes: For caregiving: conversation-style — 'How old is your child?', 'What hours do you need?', 'Any allergies or special needs we should know about?'. For cleaning: 'What type of property?', 'How many bedrooms?', 'Any specialist requirements (carpet, oven cleaning)?'. Anonymous clients can book with just a name and phone number.

nodes.name: Initiate Booking Flow
nodes.purpose: Start the booking conversation — determine if the visitor is logged in, anonymous, or new — and route to the appropriate flow.
nodes.ux_intent: Zero friction: 'Book a nanny' button → instantly shows the first question. No login wall.
nodes.vertical_notes: Anonymous users are welcomed: 'No account needed — just tell us what you need.'

nodes.name: Collect Service Details
nodes.purpose: Gather the service-specific details needed to match a worker — service type, date/time, location, and any caregiving/cleaning specifics — through a conversational multi-step form.
nodes.ux_intent: Each question appears one at a time with smart defaults. The user never feels overwhelmed — just a steady rhythm of simple choices.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nanny: ask about child ages (determines which credentials are required), care type (live-out, overnight, emergency), any medical needs (asthma, allergies, disabilities). Cleaning: property size auto-calculates estimated duration. Deep clean vs regular domestic changes the question flow.
open_questions: Should we show an estimated price during the booking flow?

nodes.name: Collect Client Contact Details
nodes.purpose: Capture the minimum contact details needed to confirm the booking — name, phone, and/or email — without requiring account creation.
nodes.ux_intent: Just two fields: 'Your name' and 'Best number to reach you'. That's it. We'll handle the rest.
nodes.vertical_notes: For caregiving: the parent's name and number. For cleaning: the property manager's or homeowner's contact. Optional: 'Create an account to track this booking and future bookings.'

nodes.name: Confirm and Submit Booking
nodes.purpose: Show a summary of the booking details and submit it as a ServiceRequest — either as an authenticated client or anonymously.
nodes.ux_intent: A clean summary card: 'Here's what we've got.' One 'Confirm Booking' button. Then an instant confirmation screen with a reference number.
nodes.vertical_notes: Anon clients receive a confirmation SMS/email: 'Your booking #REF1234 is confirmed. We'll be in touch within 2 hours to let you know who we're sending.'

nodes.name: SEO & Discoverability
nodes.purpose: Ensure the agency's public pages are fully indexed and rank well for relevant searches — so parents searching 'nanny agency London' or 'end-of-tenancy cleaner Birmingham' find them.
nodes.ux_intent: The agency owner just fills in their content — SEO is handled automatically. They don't need to understand meta tags.
nodes.vertical_notes: Target keywords: 'DBS-checked nanny [city]', 'live-in nanny agency [city]', 'end-of-tenancy cleaning [city]', 'Ofsted-registered nanny'. Structured data: LocalBusiness schema, Employee schema for workers.

nodes.name: Generate Sitemap
nodes.purpose: Auto-generate and update the sitemap.xml for all public pages whenever content is published.
nodes.ux_intent: Completely automatic — admin never thinks about sitemaps.
inputs: public pages list: homepage, worker directory, individual worker profiles

nodes.name: Generate OG Images
nodes.purpose: Auto-generate Open Graph preview images for the agency homepage and each worker's public profile — used when links are shared on WhatsApp, social media, etc.
nodes.ux_intent: When a parent shares a worker's profile on WhatsApp, it renders as a rich, professional-looking card — not a blank link.
nodes.vertical_notes: OG image for a worker: their name, photo, star rating, DBS badge, agency logo. Creates immediate trust when shared.
